account:
Today I have encountered an unusually repetitive and vague report about a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Several townsfolk have repeated nearly identical words, but none has explained an actual change or identified an original source. One account names baker, innkeeper and neighbour as having been at the bakery. That places them in the circulating story; it does not establish what they discussed. Neighbour told me freight was busy with deliveries and baker wanted bread for a gathering arranged beforehand. Innkeeper has been carrying a sack of bread, according to Townsfolk 08. These details suggest preparations for a gathering, though I do not know its purpose or whether the bridge and port rumour has any real connection.

Innkeeper repeatedly asked secretary to confirm my great hall inspection at eighteen today. Secretary said I had approved it and would meet builder at the hall entrance at seventeen fifty-five. I have now explicitly confirmed that appointment. Innkeeper says the hall will be ready for me. A gathering and preparations at the hall could be connected, and the inspection might be a reason to bring me there, but that remains speculation. I have no evidence of wrongdoing or of a deliberate effort to exclude me.

My scheduled mill inspection established only that its stall chest contained eighty-eight hay bales and eighty emeralds, with a posted price of two emeralds per bale. No custodian was identified, and quality and delivery records remain unverified. Secretary has acknowledged those limits. I kept my noon visit home and have just reached town hall for the thirteen o'clock council letters appointment. Baker is outside, and secretary is farther inside. I should keep my appointments while seeking concrete, first-hand explanations rather than treating repeated rumours as confirmed news.
